v2.evidence: Left product photograph has a gradual, natural cream-toned transition into the right-side shop name and filled vermilion information CTA.

v3.evidence: Large framed dorayaki image has a clean hard edge and a large four-character vertical title to its right, with a smaller underlined text link.

dimensions.rationale: The v3 wordmark is more memorable, but the v2 photo integration feels less like a disconnected image block; neither is unambiguously superior.

v2.evidence: Two generous and separately captioned product photographs show both seasonal namagashi and tsubu-an dorayaki as the central merchandise.

v3.evidence: A single smaller namagashi photograph follows a large description sentence, while three thin horizontal strokes occupy otherwise unused space.

dimensions.rationale: The v2 makes both foods easier to browse; the v3 sentence-led editorial intention is promising but sacrifices product visibility.

v2.evidence: Elegant neutral Mincho name and a warm accent button, but the same two-column pattern could be reused across many shop types.

v3.evidence: The vertical Japanese name takes up an unusually strong single column and the near-monochrome palette creates a more distinctive first impression.

dimensions.rationale: The v3 uses the specific four-kanji identity more assertively, while still needing verification that vertical writing is attractive in actual CSS.

v2.evidence: The page repeats a hero image, an equal two-product-photo row, and a straightforward factual ledger without much change in editorial pace.

v3.evidence: The page leads with a tall title and photo, changes to sentence plus inset photo, then ends with the information ledger.

dimensions.rationale: The second image is de-emphasised too much, but the deliberate variation between sections is a useful improvement over uniformly sized cards.

v2.evidence: Four rows of hours, closed days, address and phone are aligned clearly; the table occupies a soft background block.

v3.evidence: The same four business facts are in an orderly narrow ledger on a pale surface, with clear thin dividers.

dimensions.rationale: Both pages make operational facts legible; neither transforms this necessary factual section into an unusually distinctive visual ending.
Only tall 1024-by-1536 desktop design comps were examined; there is no evidence of a responsive 390px implementation for either candidate.
No rendered v3 page or font-metrics verification was supplied here; desktop comp pixels cannot prove reproducibility or CSS quality at target widths.

unresolved_risks.issue: Vertical Mincho glyph metrics may collapse on the real implementation target.
unresolved_risks.proposed_remedy: Keep title layout distinctive but require a vetted Japanese vertical-font stack; do not substitute artificial single-character boxes.
unresolved_risks.how_to_verify: Run 1440px and 390px browser captures and blocking glyph-order, overlap and overflow tests after the narrow vertical_name capability is approved.

unresolved_risks.issue: The v3 products section is visually sparse and does not feature both confection categories equally.
unresolved_risks.proposed_remedy: Combine v3's editorial caption rhythm with two distinct high-quality confection visuals of unequal size and fact-grounded labels.
unresolved_risks.how_to_verify: On a single screen capture, review whether both products can be identified visually without invented product names or empty filler.

unresolved_risks.issue: Neither preview demonstrates the future site's mobile composition or visual fidelity.
unresolved_risks.proposed_remedy: Specify a deliberately recomposed 390px layout before commissioning the next image, and avoid treating desktop aspect scaling as responsive design.
unresolved_risks.how_to_verify: Review actual Playwright 390px/1440px screenshots against the approved mockup and a documented mobile order.

unresolved_risks.issue: The preview PNG bytes differ from the original local WSL report hashes.
unresolved_risks.proposed_remedy: Use previews for visual critique only; use the original Codex WSL PNG and matching report and facts for formal comp intake.
unresolved_risks.how_to_verify: Compare original file sha256 to each WSL report before any signed bundle intake; never label a chat PNG as verified_original.

keep_from_v2: Product-first visual appetite: two concept confection photos should each have a meaningful clear role.
Maintain the calm soft photo-to-paper transition where it strengthens hierarchy, not as an imitation of any reference website.
Keep readable, factual captions so browsing the product offer is effortless.
keep_from_v3: Use expressive Japanese Mincho typography and a shop-specific name treatment instead of a generic heading.
Use editorial variation between hero, storytelling and business-information sections rather than three rigid repeat blocks.
Keep the restrained cream/ink/azuki palette and a quieter but obvious information link.
improve: Hero needs integrated photographic and type composition, not a giant name automatically occupying a third of the page.
Use two differing image scales and one evidence-grounded large description sentence; no fake products, meaningless placeholder strokes or filler.
End the page with intentional typographic organisation of verified business facts, rather than extra decorative effects.
Describe a 390px mobile reflow independently from the desktop comp before implementation or an additional image call.
Separate aesthetic judgment from hard-fail fact verification and measured HTML/CSS fidelity; 23/25 alone cannot establish improvement.
proof_before_implementation: Original WSL PNG/report SHA pair checked for the selected comp, with image asset approvals tracked separately.
Formal five-criterion evaluation with original ≥22/25 and every item ≥4, plus no hard fails, owner confirmed.
Independent actual 1440px and 390px render checks, including vertical Japanese font metrics and protected facts.
Owner visually confirms the trade-off between brand impression and product browsing before publication.
